question: Should a machine plan the whole idea first, like a person does, before it writes the words?
reflection: When machines learn to think from the big picture down to the details, they may help us do the same.

sources.subject: New AI Architecture Challenges Token-by-Token Generation

one_line: Stanford researchers show a model that sketches the overall meaning of an answer first and fills in detail later, generating text many times faster than similar methods.

top_stories.title: Stanford tests writing from outline to detail
top_stories.what: Stanford's Next-Concept Modeling builds an answer as layers of codes, from a rough outline to fine detail, and reportedly generated text 10 to 31 times faster than comparable diffusion models in small-scale tests.
top_stories.why: Faster, more consistent generation could cut the cost of large text tasks such as coding open-ended survey answers or summarising interviews.

top_stories.title: Speed buys quality by comparing many drafts
top_stories.what: Because the method is fast, it can produce several candidate answers and pick the one most similar to the rest, which improved summary quality in the paper's tests.
top_stories.why: Generating several drafts and choosing the consensus is a simple quality check that research teams can already apply with today's models.

idea.title: Consensus summaries for qualitative data
idea.pitch: Summarise each interview several times with an AI model and keep the version that agrees most with the others, then check a sample by hand.
idea.first_step: Take five transcripts, generate three summaries each, and compare them with a human summary.

terms.definition: A model that writes text one small piece at a time, each piece based on everything written before it.
A model that drafts a whole block of text at once and improves it over several rounds, instead of writing word by word.

concepts.summary: Research into models that plan answers before writing them, aiming for speed and consistency.
New methods keep cutting the compute needed for each answer.
